Relevant facts:
- [Meta-ControlNet] comprises a base ControlNet and a meta-controller that modulates conditioning strength based on similarity between the concept image and front-view reference CCM [d1].
- The meta-controller takes a pair of the concept image and reference CCM as input to produce meta-control signals [d1].
- Meta-control signals are injected into the base ControlNet's down-sampling blocks and directly into the pretrained diffusion model to produce adaptive control signals [d1].
- This design addresses misaligned 3D references that vanilla ControlNet fails to handle, preventing undesirable artifacts [d1].
- [Dynamic Reference Routing] adjusts reference resolution across denoise timesteps: low resolution at high noise levels for global structure, higher resolution at low noise levels for local details [d1].

Relevant facts:
- [Meta-ControlNet] equips the model with the capability to dynamically modulate the conditioning strength of the reference model, effectively utilizing available references for improving or controlling the generation process [d2].
- The base model trained with retrieved reference often ignores the reference due to considerable similarity variation among retrieved references, which confuses the diffusion model [d2].
- [Meta-ControlNet] learning requires reference models with varying levels of similarity [d2].
- [Phidias] incorporates [meta-ControlNet], [dynamic reference routing], and [self-reference augmentations] to effectively leverage reference models with varying degrees of similarity for 3D generation [d2].
- [Meta-ControlNet] improves PSNR, SSIM, and LPIPS metrics compared to the base model in ablation studies [d2].

- Law Reform (Marriage and Divorce) Act 1976 (Act 164) applies to non-Muslims; Section 3 excludes Muslims and those married under Islamic law [d5].
- Section 51 allows civil divorce if one party converts to Islam, but the converted spouse cannot file for divorce in civil court; Islamic law terminates marriage three months post-conversion [d5].
- Men often convert to Islam, leaving wives without ancillary relief or maintenance; converted spouses may file for divorce in Shari'a courts, resulting in dual settlements [d5].
- Shari'a courts have jurisdiction only over Muslims (Schedule 9 List 2); civil courts have no jurisdiction over Shari'a law [d5].
